correctness.rationale: An unrestricted finite-support lemma is proved by building all conjunction trees over finite saturation Q, showing their intersection with subformula-closed support S equals Q, and checking M,N,C,K closure including the K antecedent case. The modal one-world certificate is equivalent to satisfiability in every closure model by leastness. Saturation performs at most |S| proper rounds with at most quadratic syntactic premise checks per round; the certificate is polynomial. Classical propositional SAT/TAUT embeds without modalities. Seeded finite tests over all sixteen axiom combinations pass 394 term-bounded comparisons and 391 independent Horn enumerations; those checks are distinguished from proof.

Searches for syntactic/no-RE/no-Gen variants and overlap records returned no stronger covering statement; absolute priority is not claimed.
residual_risks: The subformula-restricted closure method is anticipated in Nishimura 2026; value lies specifically in sharp complexity and uniform polynomial certificate, not claiming that method alone is new.
Older unindexed work on noncongruential syntactic logics may contain an equivalent NP/coNP result; absence in searches cannot certify uniqueness.

value.rationale: Nishimura 2026 explicitly leaves complexity determination as a future issue and establishes only primitive-recursive decidability. Tight NP/coNP decision bounds for the entire 16-system axiomatic lattice answer the natural gap and expose the consequential absence of RE: conjunction aggregation does not force PSPACE under genuinely syntax-sensitive closure. The polynomial finite-support certificate is constructive and uniform.
